children: Traders on Binance are now paying to bet against Bitcoin. That rarely happens, and the last time it did was in June 2026.
CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost flagged the shift. He says negative Bitcoin funding on the world's largest crypto exchange may signal an early market reversal.
On or around October 15, the funding rate on Binance's Bitcoin perpetual futures fell to -0.0073%. That marked the first negative reading since June 2026.
Perpetual futures are derivative contracts with no expiry date, so exchanges use a periodic payment called the funding rate to keep their price tied to spot Bitcoin.
When the rate is positive, traders betting on higher prices (longs) pay those betting on lower prices (shorts). When it turns negative, the direction reverses and shorts pay longs.
The neutral setting sits at roughly 0.01%. A reading of -0.0073% falls below that baseline, meaning bearish positions have crowded the trade enough that they are now footing the bill.
The funding flip did not appear out of nowhere. It arrived during a sell-off that left Bitcoin trading about 56.3% below its all-time high.
As of November 22, 2026, Bitcoin had shed roughly 17.4% in November alone.
Crypto was not suffering in isolation, either. The Nasdaq has fallen more than 20%, a decline that places tech stocks in the same risk-off mood weighing on digital assets.
US inflation came in hotter than expected, which has lifted expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise rates in December 2026. Odds of a 25 basis point hike that month stood at 88.6%.
Darkfost and other analysts have pointed to previous stretches when negative funding preceded upward moves in Bitcoin's price.

The clearest example cited is the run from approximately $28,000 in October 2023 to approximately $57,000 in September 2024. Similar funding conditions accompanied that climb, which roughly doubled Bitcoin's price over the period.

There is an important caveat. The track record of this signal is mixed, and its usefulness has varied across past cycles. Negative funding is a reading of how traders feel, not a guarantee of what prices will do next.
On one side is positioning. Bearish bets are heavy enough on Binance that shorts are paying longs, and that type of lopsided positioning has historically set the stage for sharp rebounds.
On the other side is macro. Rising inflation expectations and the strong possibility of a December rate hike represent real headwinds.
A few things are worth watching from here.
First, the persistence of the negative reading. A single dip to -0.0073% is a data point. Funding that stays negative across several weeks would carry more weight as a sentiment indicator.
Second, the inflation and rate picture heading into December. With odds of a hike at 88.6%, much of that outcome may already be priced in.
Third, the correlation with equities. As long as Bitcoin keeps trading in step with a falling Nasdaq, crypto-specific signals like funding rates may struggle to drive prices on their own.

title: Binance Bitcoin funding turns negative, and one analyst sees a possible reversal
